rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER
rows.read_by: Fake `perfetto` script that the test writes (`perfetto/test_perfetto.py`)
rows.values: Path of a file. The script only tests that the path exists.
rows.default: Unset: no wait for a file. With `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT` not empty, the fake `perfetto` sleeps for `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_DELAY` seconds and then exits.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `perfetto` wait until this file exists before it exits with status `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT`.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT` is not empty. The wait has no time limit. One test passes the path of `killall.args` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_NOTIFY_STATUS
rows.read_by: Fake `perfetto` script that the test writes (`perfetto/test_perfetto.py`)
rows.values: The text `0` means success. Any other non-empty text means failure. The script compares text and does not parse a number.
rows.default: Unset: counts as `0`. The fake `perfetto` reports readiness success.
rows.effect: Selects whether the fake `perfetto` reports readiness success or readiness failure on the `--notify-fd` descriptor.
rows.notes: With `0` the script writes a byte of value 0 and creates `perfetto.ready` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. With other text it writes a byte of value 1 and exits with status `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT`. That status is 1 when `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT` is empty.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_QUERY_HANG
rows.read_by: Fake `perfetto` script that the test writes (`perfetto/test_perfetto.py`)
rows.values: Any non-empty text enables it. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. A `--query` call of the fake `perfetto` returns.
rows.effect: A `--query` call of the fake `perfetto` never returns.
rows.notes: The fake `perfetto` creates `query.called` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory on each `--query` call. One test checks that this file does not exist after a run of the launcher script `perfetto/tronperf`.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_SERVICE_ERROR
rows.read_by: Fake `perfetto` script that the test writes (`perfetto/test_perfetto.py`)
rows.values: Any non-empty text enables it. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `perfetto` prints `Connected to the Perfetto tracing service`.
rows.effect: The fake `perfetto` prints `Service error: Duplicate buffer name` in place of the connected message.
rows.notes: The script still writes the readiness byte. Then it waits until `runtron.args` or `killall.args` exists in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. Then it exits with status 0. One test checks that both launcher scripts fail and that this file does not exist.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_SKIP_NOTIFY
rows.read_by: Fake `perfetto` script that the test writes (`perfetto/test_perfetto.py`)
rows.values: Any non-empty text enables it. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `perfetto` writes the readiness byte.
rows.effect: The fake `perfetto` writes no readiness byte to the `--notify-fd` descriptor.
rows.notes: The script then does not create `perfetto.ready` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. `FAKE_PERFETTO_NOTIFY_STATUS` then has no effect. One test sets it with `TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT` set to `1` (1 second). It checks that the launcher script `perfetto/wrapper` exits with status 1.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_WAIT_FOR_PROBE_EXIT
rows.read_by: Fake `perfetto` script that the test writes (`perfetto/test_perfetto.py`)
rows.values: Any non-empty text enables it. The script does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: off. The fake `perfetto` does not wait.
rows.effect: Makes the fake `perfetto` wait until the fake `traced_probes` process has ended before it reports readiness.
rows.notes: The script reads the process id from `traced_probes.pid` in the `FAKE_STATE` directory. It stops waiting when `/proc/<pid>/stat` is not readable, or when that file shows the state `Z` (a process that has exited).

new_terms.definition: A short script that a test writes in place of a real program, for example `perfetto`, `runtron`, `sudo`, `git` or `gh`. The test puts it where the code under test looks for the real program. It is not a file of the repository.
The three Perfetto programs that the launcher scripts start, in this order: the tracing service, the daemon that registers data sources, and the client that writes the trace file.

The two launcher scripts for Perfetto traces. `perfetto/tronperf` starts the Perfetto programs and then runtron. `perfetto/wrapper` starts the Perfetto programs and can send `SIGUSR1` to a running process.
One byte that a Perfetto program writes to the notify descriptor to report that it is ready.
The file descriptor on which a Perfetto program reports readiness. `TRACED_NOTIFY_FD` and `TRACED_PROBES_NOTIFY_FD` name it for the two daemons. The option `--notify-fd` names it for `perfetto`.
The kernel tracing file system. The launcher scripts use `/sys/kernel/tracing`.

notes: All 24 variables are fixtures (hand_set false, group fixture). Only fake programs that two test files write read them. No row is dropped. FAKE_TRACED_CLOSE_READY_FD has an empty set_in: the fake traced script reads it and no test in the checkout sets it. Four evidence quotes are a contiguous part of their source line, not the whole line. The whole line holds the shell operator made of two pipe characters, and no field may hold a pipe character. The four are the read sites of FAKE_SUDO_FAIL, FAKE_SUDO_NO_EFFECT, FAKE_SUDO_RACE (second evidence object) and FAKE_TRACED_HOLD_READY_FD (first evidence object). All other quotes are the whole line without the indent. Fixture rows also carry values and default, taken from the script text.
